item.title: Google launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15‑second native video and lower price
item.description:
Google launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15‑second native video and lower price

Today, Google is rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business.

🔍 Overview

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash adds native 15‑second video creation, multi‑turn conversational editing, and stronger reference following.

🛠️ Features

  • Native video generation up to 15 seconds (up from 10 seconds) with one‑second granularity from 3 – 15 seconds.
  • Multi‑turn conversational editing works across full clips, allowing background swaps, lighting changes, aspect‑ratio adjustments, or product swaps turn by turn without re‑generating the entire clip.
  • Enhanced reference following keeps faces, garments, packaging typography, brand colors, and lighting consistent across camera angles and motion.
  • Supports input of character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to 3 seconds), and audio cues; the model retains those details throughout generation.
  • Generates more fluid continuous camera movements—such as sweeping FPV fly‑throughs and dramatic zoom‑outs—with significantly fewer jump cuts.
  • Produces clearer lip‑sync, natural‑sounding dialogue, and distinct multi‑speaker conditioning.

📏 Duration, Resolution & Pricing

  • Max video length: 15 seconds (previously 10 seconds).
  • Duration can be set in one‑second increments between 3 and 15 seconds.
  • Drafts can be created at 360p or 720p; final clips can be upscaled to 1080p or 4K.
  • Price reduced 30 % from Omni 1.1, now $0.07 per second for 720p video.

🎞️ Consistency & Editing

  • Faces, garments, and branding stay consistent across camera angles; e.g., a single model photo plus front‑and‑back shots of three outfits generates a 15‑second virtual try‑on sequence with consistent identity and garment details.
  • Less visual drift or morphing when interpolating between keyframes or extending clips.
  • Multi‑turn edits can change background turn by turn (e.g., striped pavilion tent → oak forest → stable with a white horse → market fair → stone castle) while preserving character performance, armor reflections, and framing.
  • Reference matching improved: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash builds layered posters sequentially, locking material, shadow, and typographic details through the final frame.

🚀 Availability & Infrastructure

  • First time Gemini Omni is generally available, backed by Google Cloud’s enterprise‑grade infrastructure and security.
  • Provisioned Throughput is offered; outputs include an imperceptible SynthID watermark.
  • Ongoing development targets fast sports action, rapid script changes, and complex physics, but the current version is ready for businesses, developers, and creators producing videos at scale.

💡 Use Cases & Adoption

  • Businesses, startups, and creatives are already integrating Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash into workflows.
  • Applicable for multi‑character dialogue in Flow, video explainers in Gemini for business, and polished avatar‑driven videos with music and narration in Google Vids.
  • Enables efficient production of product explainers, social ad spots, virtual try‑on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads.

#GeminiOmni #VideoAI #GoogleAI #GenerativeMedia

Source: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips

item.title: OpenMontage: First Open‑Source Agentic Video Production System
item.description:
OpenMontage: First Open‑Source Agentic Video Production System

The open‑source community released OpenMontage, described as the world’s first open‑source, agentic video production system.

🔍 Overview

  • World’s first open‑source, agentic video production system.
  • Provides 12 production pipelines, over 100 tools, and more than 700 agent skill and production‑knowledge files.
  • Turns an AI coding assistant into a full video production studio.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent builds a corpus from free stock footage and open archives.
  • It retrieves actual motion clips, edits them into a timeline, and renders a finished piece.
  • OpenMontage can make image‑based videos and also make a real video video for free/open‑source workflows.

⚙️ Key details

  • License: AGPLv3.
  • Website: https://openmontage.video.
  • Follow The Build.

🎬 Showcase productions

Production Length Style / Highlights Cost
SIGNAL FROM TOMORROW — Cinematic sci‑fi trailer; concept, script, scene plan, Veo‑generated motion clips, soundtrack, Remotion composition —
THE LAST BANANA 60 s Pixar‑style animated short; 6 Kling v3‑generated motion clips (via fal.ai), Google Chirp3‑HD narration, royalty‑free piano music, TikTok‑style word‑level captions, Remotion composition $1.33
OBJECTS IN OVERDRIVE 54 s Music‑driven 3D showcase; ten objects with distinct choreography (gravity‑shifting furniture, frozen car drifts, cloth impacts, refractive lenses, moving gears, acrobatic robot, and more); custom Blender animation & physics, kinetic typography, phonk soundtrack; rendered with Blender Eevee/Cycles and assembled with FFmpeg; no narration —
Reimagine Your Universe 50 s Vertical transformation film; five generated motion scenes, sparse Google Chirp narration, Pixabay score, HyperFrames composition linking separate clips into one authored cinematic journey about $4
Products Come to Life 60 s Product film built from approved hero stills; five hard‑surface products separate into their own engineering and reassemble, each still pinned as the first and last frame so the model invents motion without losing product identity; image‑to‑video generation, bespoke sound, narration, custom composition —
Imagine the Possibilities with OpenMontage — Seven generated worlds collected into one music‑only showcase; three image models supply campaign, fashion, and miniature‑world artwork; four video models expand the journey through architecture, material transformation, a living greenhouse, and a creature encounter —

🚀 Availability

OpenMontage is released under the AGPLv3 license and can be accessed at https://openmontage.video.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables free/open‑source video creation pipelines that combine stock‑footage retrieval, AI‑generated motion clips, and open‑source rendering tools.
  • Demonstrates end‑to‑end production—from concept to final render—at costs as low as $1.33 for a 60‑second short.

#OpenMontage #OpenSource #AIProduction #VideoGeneration

Source: calesthio/OpenMontage

item.title: AI-Powered 1980s Portrait Trend Transforms Social Media Nostalgia
item.description:
AI-Powered 1980s Portrait Trend Transforms Social Media Nostalgia

Users are utilizing AI to transform ordinary selfies and family photographs into polished 1980s-era portraits, characterized by voluminous hair, oversized silhouettes, analogue textures, and dramatic studio lighting.

🧩 How it works

What started as individual experimentation with ChatGPT has evolved into a social-media movement. Users employ AI filters or image-generation prompts to:

  • Recreate themselves and their families.
  • Create imagined versions of their younger selves.
  • Construct a version of the past, regardless of whether they lived through the era.

💡 Why it matters

AI is making nostalgia participatory by turning a culturally inherited aesthetic into something immediately playable and shareable. This is particularly relevant for younger audiences who associate the 80s with retro television, old Bollywood imagery, and vintage family albums rather than personal memory.

This trend illustrates a growing premium on cultural speed, where formats can have lifespans measured in days or hours. AI accelerates the process of moving from an organic social behavior to a format amplified by creators and adopted by brands.

⚙️ Key details

Various brands have adapted the 80s visual language for their social content by finding behaviors consumers are already participating in.

Brand Application of Trend
Maggi, Cadbury, Parle Hide & Seek, Haldiram’s Connects visual treatment to emotional territories of childhood, family, and school.
Libas The aesthetic itself becomes the content.
Instamart Adapted 80s visual language for social content.

#AI #GenerativeAI #SocialMediaTrends #DigitalNostalgia #ChatGPT

Source: Jungle Book Studio picks up international sales for ‘Angh’

item.title: Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support
item.description:
Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support

Suno has launched v6, its first AI music model developed with support from the record industry. The model is being rolled out starting today, and Suno intends to eventually retire its previous models.

🧩 How it works

According to Suno’s Jack Brody, v6 was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on.”

Training data includes:

  • Content licensed from partners Believe, BMG, and Warner Music Group
  • “User data”

It remains unclear if the training data is completely free of dubiously obtained content.

⚙️ Key details

Suno v6 consists of three different models:

Model Description
v6-mini Available for free to all; focused on fast, resource-light creation. Results are simpler and often contain more artifacts.
v6-wild Designed for “happy accidents and natural imperfections.”
v6 The standard model.

Capabilities and Performance

  • Genre Understanding: All three models show dramatic improvement in understanding genres, accurately capturing the superficial hallmarks of styles such as “krautrock” or “hyperpop.”
  • Multimodal Prompts: Users are no longer limited to text; v6 can create tracks based on video, images, or other audio.
  • Editing and Mashups: Users can now use plain language within a chat to edit specific parts of a song, such as a single lyric or guitar line, without regenerating the entire track. The model can also combine multiple elements from a user’s Suno library into new creations.

Limitations

  • Human Imperfections: The model cannot capture “natural imperfections.” Attempts to produce dissonant, off-key, or out-of-tune results—including “out-of-tune piano played haphazardly”—have failed.
  • Prompt Adherence: v6 may ignore specific prompts, such as requests for “no drums” or “monotone vocals.”
  • AI Artifacts: Vocals in v6 may produce more harsh-edged artifacts common to AI models than those found in v5.

🚀 Availability

Suno v6 starts rolling out today.

#Suno #AImusic #GenerativeAI #MusicIndustry

Source: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help
